question: The Chandrayaan-2 mission consisted of an orbiter, a lander named __________, and a rover named ___________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vikram, Pragyan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Chandrayaan-2** was India's second lunar exploration mission developed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**.

• The mission consisted of three components: an **Orbiter**, a **Lander** named **Vikram**, and a **Rover** named **Pragyan**.

• The **Lander Vikram** was named after Dr. Vikram Sarabhai, the father of the Indian space program.

• The **Rover Pragyan** (meaning 'wisdom' in Sanskrit) was designed to analyze the lunar surface and send data back to Earth.

• The mission aimed to explore the **South Polar Region of the Moon**, which had not been extensively studied by previous missions.

• **ISRO launched Chandrayaan-2** on **22 July 2019** from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota using the GSLV Mk III rocket.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Orbiter:**

• The **Orbiter** was equipped with eight scientific instruments to study the Moon from its orbit.

• It continues to function and provides valuable data about the lunar surface, atmosphere, and mineral composition.

• The orbiter's mission life was originally intended to be one year but has been extended due to its efficient fuel usage.

• **Lander Vikram:**

• The **Lander Vikram** was designed to perform a soft landing on the Moon's surface.

• Unfortunately, the lander lost communication with ISRO during its final descent, around 2.1 kilometers above the lunar surface.

• Despite this setback, the mission was considered a significant achievement for India's space exploration efforts.

• **Rover Pragyan:**

• The **Rover Pragyan** had a mission life of 14 Earth days and was equipped with two instruments to study the lunar soil and terrain.

• Its goal was to analyze the chemical composition of the Moon's surface and detect elements such as magnesium, aluminum, and silicon.

• However, it could not perform its tasks as the lander did not successfully deploy it on the lunar surface.

• **Significance of Chandrayaan-2:**

• The mission demonstrated India's capability to design, launch, and operate complex space missions.

• It contributed valuable insights into lunar science and enhanced India's reputation in the global space community.

• The data from the Orbiter continues to be used for scientific research and analysis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Chandrayaan-1:**

• India's first lunar mission, Chandrayaan-1, was launched on **22 October 2008**.

• It discovered water molecules on the Moon, a groundbreaking finding in lunar science.

• **Future Lunar Missions:**

• ISRO is planning Chandrayaan-3, which will focus on achieving a successful soft landing on the Moon.

• The mission will include a lander and a rover, but no orbiter, as the Chandrayaan-2 orbiter is still operational.

• **Global Lunar Exploration:**

• Countries like the USA, Russia, and China have conducted successful lunar exploration missions.

• India's effort places it among the elite group of nations actively studying the Moon.
